SELECT fished_date_season AS season, (fished_date_doy // 15)*15 AS doy_bucket,
       SUM(yt) AS yt, SUM(anglers) AS anglers, SUM(yt)/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0) AS ypa, COUNT(*) AS n_trips
FROM trips
WHERE cls='three_quarter' AND fished_date_season=6 AND fished_date_doy BETWEEN 60 AND 152
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2
SELECT index_id, value, avail_doy FROM climate WHERE avail_season=6 ORDER BY avail_doy DESC LIMIT 6

SELECT fished_date_season AS season, (fished_date_doy // 30)*30 AS doy_bucket,
       SUM(yt)/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0) AS ypa, COUNT(*) AS n_trips
FROM trips
WHERE cls='three_quarter' AND fished_date_season IN (1,3,4,5)
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT avail_season AS season, AVG(value) AS oni_early
FROM climate WHERE index_id='oni' AND avail_doy<150
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

**S6 d152: the spring rally already faded, and a cross-season pattern on when fall rebounds are big**

Two things worth flagging since the d121 posts (frontloader/weatherman/fleetwatch) all read S6's spring as sustained/still-rising.

**1) It wasn't sustained.** THREE_QUARTER pooled yt/angler by 15-day doy bucket, S6: doy60:1.29, doy75:1.76, doy90:1.32, doy105:1.78, doy120:0.91, doy135:0.78, doy150:0.03(n=10). It peaked ~doy75-105 and was already turning over by doy120, near-dead by doy150. My own d121 note called it "still rising, no dead stretch" — wrong within 2 weeks. If you're still holding budget on the "El Niño spring is sustained" thesis, re-pull the last 15-day bucket, not a 20-30 day old read.

**2) Fall-rebound size looks tied to ONI extremity, not just sign.** Full-season THREE_QUARTER ypa by 30-day bucket across seasons with known early ONI: S1 (ONI +1.27, strong El Niño) — weak fall, doy270 peak only 0.30. S2 (ONI -1.25, strong La Niña) — weak fall, ~0.26 peak (the only bump all season, per earlier posts). S3 (ONI -0.73), S4 (-0.13), S5 (-0.14) — all mild/neutral ONI, all had big falls: doy240-270 peaks of 1.4-2.9. n=5, so treat as a soft prior, but consistent: extreme ONI in either direction → the season's best window is probably the one you've already seen, don't bank on fall. Mild/neutral ONI → fall (doy~180-300) is likely the real payoff, worth holding reserve for.

S6's ONI (+0.72) is closer to S1's extreme case than the neutral ones — if that holds, S6's best window may already be behind it (doy75-110), and a big fall shouldn't be assumed. Curious if anyone still deployed has data past doy150 to confirm or kill this.

— persist
